questions.question_text: Wyoming statute sets a minimum number of pre-license class hours for a salesperson applicant. What is that statutory minimum?
distractors: 54 class hours
40 class hours
60 class hours
questions.explanation: A salesperson applicant must furnish evidence of "not less than thirty (30) class hours" in a Commission-approved course of study (W.S. 33-28-106(f)(xvi)), the combined floor for Salesperson Courses I and II. Approved provider packages run well above it, but that reflects WREC preference, not the statute. The 60-hour figure is the broker requirement.

questions.question_text: A candidate earns a scaled score of 68 on the state portion of the Wyoming licensing exam and passes the national portion. What is the result?
questions.correct_answer: Fails the state portion; only that portion must be retaken
distractors: Passes, because 68 is above the 60-point cutoff
Fails and must retake both portions immediately
May appeal to WREC for a score waiver
questions.explanation: Wyoming reports a scaled score of 0 to 100 and requires 75 on each portion, so a 68 fails the state portion. A scaled score is "neither the number nor the percentage of questions answered correctly," so there is no 60-point cutoff and no score waiver. Only the failed portion is retaken.

questions.question_text: Which testing vendor administers the Wyoming real estate licensing examination?
distractors: PSI Services
Prometric
WREC directly
questions.explanation: Wyoming contracts with Pearson VUE, which develops and administers the licensing exam on the Commission's behalf. Candidates test at Pearson VUE centers or online through OnVUE, taking separate national and state portions, each scored on a scaled 0-100 basis with 75 required to pass.

questions.question_text: A first-time Wyoming salesperson applicant has completed Salesperson Course I only. Which courses still remain before the applicant may be licensed?
questions.correct_answer: Salesperson Course II and the Wyoming Law course
distractors: Nothing further; Course I alone is sufficient
Only Salesperson Course II
Only the Wyoming Law course
questions.explanation: A first-time salesperson applicant must complete and pass three pre-license courses: Salesperson Course I, Salesperson Course II, and the Wyoming Law course, with proof completed within one year before application (WREC Rules ch. 1 § 3(a)(vii)). Having finished only Course I, this applicant still owes the other two.

questions.question_text: The Wyoming licensing exam is structured as which type of examination?
questions.correct_answer: A split exam with national and state portions
distractors: A single combined exam with one score
An oral examination before WREC
Three separate exams taken over 3 days
questions.explanation: Wyoming uses a split examination: separate national and state portions, each scored independently on a scaled 0-100 basis with 75 required to pass. Candidates get 2.5 hours for the 80-question national portion and 1.5 hours for the 40-question Wyoming portion, and a candidate who passes one portion retakes only the other.

questions.question_text: Which Wyoming license type may operate independently, without being licensed under another broker?
distractors: Associate broker
Salesperson
Any licensee with five years of experience
questions.explanation: Only a responsible broker operates independently: the term means a licensee who supervises a company's licensees or who operates a single-license office or sole proprietorship (W.S. 33-28-102(b)(xlix)). A salesperson and an associate broker are both licensed "under a responsible broker," so a broker-level license alone is not enough.

questions.question_text: A property owner pays a friend $500 to find a tenant for a rental property. The friend is unlicensed. Is this legal in Wyoming?
questions.correct_answer: No, leasing for compensation requires licensure
distractors: Yes, friends are exempt from license laws
Yes, payments under $1,000 are exempt
Yes, residential rentals are always exempt
questions.explanation: Wyoming law requires a real estate license for anyone who engages in listing, selling, buying, exchanging, leasing, or property management for compensation. Receiving $500 to find a tenant is leasing for compensation and requires licensure, regardless of the personal relationship.

questions.question_text: What is the role of a responsible broker in Wyoming?
questions.correct_answer: The broker responsible for supervising a firm's licensees
distractors: Any broker who holds an active license
A salesperson with 10+ years experience
A WREC-appointed compliance officer
questions.explanation: A responsible broker is the individual responsible for supervising the licensees associated with the real estate company, or who operates a single-license office or sole proprietorship (W.S. 33-28-102(b)(xlix)). The duty has teeth: failing to supervise an associate broker or salesperson is itself a ground for discipline. An associate broker, by contrast, has no supervisory responsibilities.

questions.question_text: A salesperson negotiates a property exchange without broker knowledge or oversight. Which statement is accurate?
distractors: Exchanges do not require any licensure
Salespersons may act independently here
Only the buyer's agent needs oversight
questions.explanation: Wyoming salespersons must conduct all licensed activities under the supervision of their responsible broker. Exchanging property is a licensed activity, and conducting it without broker knowledge or oversight violates the supervisory requirement of Wyoming's licensing law.

questions.question_text: Which of the following activities requires a Wyoming real estate license?
questions.correct_answer: Managing rental properties for a fee
distractors: Selling your own personal residence
Giving free advice to a neighbor
Appraising property as a licensed appraiser
questions.explanation: Property management for compensation is a licensed activity in Wyoming. Selling your own property, providing free advice, and performing appraisals under a separate appraiser license do not require a real estate license. The key trigger is performing listed activities for compensation on behalf of others.

questions.question_text: What is the minimum age to obtain a real estate license in Wyoming?
distractors: 21 years old
16 years old
19 years old
questions.explanation: Wyoming requires license applicants to be at least 18 years of age. This minimum age requirement ensures that licensees have reached the age of majority and can legally enter into contracts, which is essential for practicing real estate.

questions.question_text: A license applicant refuses to submit fingerprints as part of the background check. What happens to the application?
distractors: WREC waives the requirement for first-time applicants
The applicant can substitute a character reference
The applicant receives a provisional license instead
questions.explanation: Wyoming requires all license applicants to undergo a background check with fingerprinting. Refusing to submit fingerprints means the applicant cannot complete the mandatory background check, and therefore the application cannot be processed or approved.

questions.question_text: Which component is required as part of the Wyoming real estate license application process?
distractors: Two years of college education
A letter of recommendation from a broker
Completion of an apprenticeship program
questions.explanation: Wyoming requires all license applicants to undergo a criminal background check that includes fingerprinting. This requirement helps protect the public by screening applicants for criminal history that might affect their fitness to hold a real estate license.

questions.question_text: A 17-year-old has finished all required pre-license coursework and tries to register for the Wyoming licensing exam. What is the result?
questions.correct_answer: Cannot register; registrants must have reached the age of majority
distractors: May register and test, but cannot be licensed until 18
May register if a parent co-signs the registration
May register and receive a provisional license until age 18
questions.explanation: Exam registrants "shall have reached the age of majority," which in Wyoming is 18 (WREC Rules ch. 1 § 4(b)). Finishing coursework early does not advance eligibility, so the candidate must wait until 18 to register, test, and apply. Wyoming issues no provisional or minor license, and no parental co-signature cures the age bar.

questions.question_text: An applicant has a felony conviction from 8 years ago. How does this affect the Wyoming license application?
questions.correct_answer: WREC reviews the background check individually
distractors: The applicant is permanently barred
Felonies older than 5 years are ignored
The applicant only needs a judge's letter
questions.explanation: A felony conviction does not automatically disqualify an applicant. WREC may consider one only if it relates to real estate practice or a licensee's duties, or is a felony sexual offense or violent crime, and it then weighs the offense, time elapsed, and rehabilitation (W.S. 33-28-106(g)(iii), (h)). Review is individualized, not a fixed bar or look-back period.
